pros: Task-centric design aligns with agent workflow (most agents execute tasks)
JSONL format makes large logs searchable with simple grep (no database needed)
Learnings.md provides human-readable narrative that's easy to scan
Separation of structured (JSONL) and narrative (MD) optimizes for different access patterns
Context cache reduces redundant lookups while TTL prevents staleness
Relationships.json enables trust-based delegation without central coordination
Team-specific extensions allow specialization without bloating common schema
Works naturally with Claude SDK tools (Read, Grep, Glob)
Scales to 100+ agents (each agent's memory is independent)
Easy to implement (file-based, no infrastructure dependencies)
Supports both structured queries (grep) and semantic search (read full learnings)
Integrates cleanly with Task tool delegation pattern
Compatible with planned message bus architecture
Constitutional compliance built-in (Article III memory protocol)
Low cognitive overhead for agents (simple file structure)
Version control friendly (text files can be git-tracked)
cons: No full-text search across all memories (would need grep -r which is slower)
JSONL format requires parsing each line (not instant random access)
Consolidation requires agent discipline (may need auditor enforcement)
Relationship scores can become stale if not actively maintained
Context cache TTL is arbitrary (7 days may not fit all use cases)
No automatic deduplication of learnings (agent must manually consolidate)
Grep performance degrades with very large files (>100K lines)
Requires agents to remember to update memories (not automatic)
Cross-agent memory search is slower than single-agent search
No transactional guarantees (concurrent writes could corrupt JSONL)
Learning quality depends on agent's ability to synthesize insights
Relationships.json structure may need versioning as schema evolves
No built-in mechanism for agents to request others' memories proactively
Task log can be verbose if agents do many micro-tasks
Memory consolidation creates unavailability window (file rewrite)
No automatic knowledge transfer when agent is retired

vs_no_memory.disadvantage: None - memory is essential for learning

conclusion: Team 2 proposes a pragmatic, task-centric memory architecture that balances simplicity with functionality. By using JSONL for structured logs, Markdown for narrative learnings, and JSON for relationships, we optimize for the tools agents have (Read, Grep, Glob) while scaling to 100+ agents. The key innovation is self-consolidating memory that prevents bloat through TTL, summarization, and decay. This approach integrates naturally with the Task tool delegation pattern and planned message bus, while maintaining constitutional compliance. The design is biased toward action: agents can immediately search memories before tasks, learn from experience, and improve collaboration through relationship tracking. We believe this strikes the right balance between sophisticated memory and operational simplicity.
